title: R' Tanchum of Noy
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Shabbat 30a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.30a.3) introduces R' Tanchum of Noy’s discourse with a question: may one extinguish a lamp for a sick person on Shabbat? Hyman describes him as opening with a teaching of Rav Yehudah in Rav's name and delivering a long discourse. He concludes, “Regarding the question I asked before you, a lamp is called a lamp,” etc. Hyman infers that he served as his town's judge and preacher.[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: The Gemara introduces the question with לעילא, “above.” [Hyman’s print, vol. III, p. 1243](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/ba/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._III._1910.pdf#page=410) also has לעילא where the supplied Hebrew has לעולא.

The discourse opens with a challenge to Solomon. It later cites [Rav Yehudah in Rav’s name](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.30a.6). [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3578&lang=en) cites the opening folio under Rabbi Tanchum of Noy.
The conclusion on [Shabbat 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.30b.2) says “the question I asked before you.” Hyman infers that Tanchum was the judge and preacher of his town.
